videos.subject: approx
videos.title: A Second Course in Algorithms (Lecture 15: Introduction to Approximation Algorithms)
videos.speaker: Tim Roughgarden
videos.scopeNote: Overview of approximation guarantees, makespan scheduling, a brief knapsack scaling summary, and the terminal-MST approximation for Steiner tree. Preparation for the assigned FPTAS, configuration PTAS and Steiner-forest proofs; it does not supply those complete proofs. The instructor's course page links this video; its associated Lecture 15 notes confirm the topic scope.

videos.subject: approx
videos.title: A Second Course in Algorithms (Lecture 17: Linear Programming and Approximation Algorithms)
videos.speaker: Tim Roughgarden
videos.scopeNote: Set-cover LP duality and dual fitting, followed by LP rounding and a primal-dual algorithm for weighted vertex cover. Directly illustrates tight-set charging in the frequency-two special case; the general frequency-f proof remains an extension. The instructor's linked Lecture 17 notes contain the primal-dual algorithm and its full charging argument.

videos.subject: approx
videos.title: A Second Course in Algorithms (Lecture 18: Five Essential Tools for Analyzing Randomized Algorithms)
videos.speaker: Tim Roughgarden
videos.scopeNote: Fair-assignment MAX-3SAT, expectation and tail inequalities, Chernoff bounds, and independent path rounding for low-congestion routing. The associated Lecture 18 notes derive logarithmic-over-loglog congestion for unit capacities and demands. It does not cover the MAX-SAT LP's 3/4 guarantee or arbitrary-demand routing without additional hypotheses.

videos.subject: approx
videos.title: A Second Course in Algorithms (Lecture 20: Semidefinite Programming and the Maximum Cut Problem)
videos.speaker: Tim Roughgarden
videos.scopeNote: Derives the vector and Gram-matrix MAX-CUT relaxation, PSD feasibility, random-hyperplane rounding, angular separation probability and the approximately 0.878 approximation. The instructor's linked Lecture 20 notes substantiate this scope. Vector-coloring semicolorings and positive-threshold Gaussian independent-set extraction are separate topics.

videos.subject: approx
videos.title: 17. Complexity: Approximation Algorithms
videos.speaker: Srinivas Devadas
videos.scopeNote: Introductory approximation ratios and PTAS/FPTAS distinctions, matching-based vertex cover, greedy set cover, and a two-way partition PTAS. The official transcript confirms these examples. Useful preparation for general identical-machine schemes and primal-dual cover, but not the assigned configuration or general-frequency proofs.

videos.subject: approx
videos.title: Approximation schemes in planar graphs: Branchwidth and Baker's technique.
videos.speaker: Shay Mozes
videos.scopeNote: MIT 6.889 Lecture 8 develops carving/branch decompositions, a planar radius-to-width bound, and Baker's technique through minimum vertex cover. It supports the structural idea behind planar MIS, but uses a different objective and decomposition presentation from the assigned proof.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: 2020.08.27 - IP#1 - Graph Non-Isomorphism & PSPACE Upper Bound
videos.speaker: Alessandro Chiesa
videos.scopeNote: Introduces interactive proofs, basic GNI and the PSPACE upper bound. Use alongside the public-transcript consistency argument and GMW's additional malicious-verifier certification; those refinements require separate study.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: Instance Checking and the Permanent: Graduate Complexity Lecture 16 at CMU
videos.speaker: Ryan O'Donnell
videos.scopeNote: Graduate treatment of permanent self-reductions and instance checking. Provides algebraic and program-checking context for LFKN; the assigned paper's complete compression protocol and consequences remain separate reading.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: Lecture 1: Interactive Proofs and the Sum-Check Protocol, Part 1
videos.speaker: Yael Tauman Kalai
videos.scopeNote: MIT graduate lecture on interactive proofs and sum-check, with #SAT listed in the official lecture description. Supports algebraic counting verification; supplement it with LFKN's permanent-specific reduction and closure arguments.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: 2020.09.03 - IP#3 - IP=PSPACE
videos.speaker: Alessandro Chiesa
videos.scopeNote: Covers QBF arithmetization and PSPACE contained in IP. The syllabus explicitly identifies Shamir's protocol with Shen's degree reduction, matching the guide's modern operator presentation.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: [CSS.203.1] Computational Complexity - Lecture 28
videos.speaker: Prahladh Harsha
videos.scopeNote: Introduces the multiprover model, fixed answer tables, MIP=NEXP and the PCP connection. The accompanying Lecture 28 notes confirm the instructor and topics; this is an overview, not the full BFL multilinearity/decoding proof.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: 2020.09.17 - IP#7 - Zero Knowledge Interactive Proofs
videos.speaker: Alessandro Chiesa
videos.scopeNote: Covers GI, honest- and malicious-verifier zero knowledge, and perfect/statistical/computational simulation notions. Supports the definitions and GI unit; the GMW NP construction and GNI certification need their own proofs.

videos.subject: complexity
videos.title: ZKP MOOC Lecture 1: Introduction and History of ZKP
videos.speaker: Shafi Goldwasser
videos.scopeNote: Historical and conceptual orientation. The official slides include GMW's graph-3-coloring commitment construction; this introduction does not replace the complete paper's cryptographic assumptions and malicious-verifier simulation analysis.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Bounded Differences Inequality (aka Azuma-Hoeffding Inequality)
videos.speaker: Yufei Zhao
videos.scopeNote: MIT 18.226 short lecture on bounded differences, with coupon-collector and random-graph chromatic-number applications. Direct support for the basic concentration mechanism; it does not replace the assigned sparse four-value chromatic-window argument.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Lecture 23: Martingales (Plain, Sub, and Super)
videos.speaker: Robert Gallager
videos.scopeNote: MIT 6.262 lecture introducing martingales, submartingales, supermartingales and stopped processes after Wald's identity. Builds the conditional-expectation vocabulary; the official description does not promise the assigned Azuma or adaptive-variance proofs.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Information Theory in Combinatorics I
videos.speaker: Shachar Lovett
videos.institution: University of California, San Diego; Simons Institute, University of California, Berkeley (host)
videos.scopeNote: Information Theory Boot Camp, January 2015. The official I–II series abstract and shared notes cover entropy, conditioning, chain rules, Shearer's lemma and combinatorial counting. Session I supplies the introduction; not every advertised I–II application is claimed to occur in this one recording.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Polar Codes I
videos.speaker: Erdal Arıkan
videos.institution: Bilkent University; Simons Institute, University of California, Berkeley (host)
videos.scopeNote: Graduate tutorial on information polarization, polar-code construction and decoding. Useful constructive channel-coding context for Shannon's theorem, rather than the book's random-coding proof. The official abstract assumes basic information theory and elementary martingales.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Correlation inequalities for Schur functions and Young tableaux
videos.speaker: Igor Pak
videos.institution: University of California, Los Angeles; Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics (IPAM)
videos.scopeNote: IPAM workshop lecture recorded April 17, 2024, listed by the institutes' official video archive and published on IPAM's channel. Research overview of FKG-type correlation inequalities and poset/algebraic applications; not a substitute for the assigned Four Functions or XYZ proofs.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Lecture 7: Szemerédi’s Graph Regularity Lemma II: Triangle Removal Lemma
videos.speaker: Yufei Zhao
videos.scopeNote: Triangle counting, the partition–clean–count method, triangle removal and the graph-theoretic proof of Roth's theorem. MIT's current course page is labeled Fall 2023, but its video gallery explicitly says these lectures were recorded for 18.217 in 2019.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Lecture 9: Szemerédi’s Graph Regularity Lemma IV: Induced Removal Lemma
videos.speaker: Yufei Zhao
videos.scopeNote: The official description covers stronger graph regularity, induced removal and graph property testing. Direct support for the structural input in Chapter 17; the exact 3-color restriction tree and semi-hereditary characterization are not asserted here. Recording is from 2019 despite the current Fall 2023 course label.

videos.subject: probability
videos.title: Property Testing for Graphs
videos.speaker: Artur Czumaj
videos.institution: University of Warwick; Simons Institute, University of California, Berkeley (host)
videos.scopeNote: Sublinear Algorithms Boot Camp lecture, May 21, 2024. A graph-testing survey to orient the Chapter 17 material; the official page does not identify it as a proof of Alon–Spencer's particular colorability tester, so that precise coverage is not claimed.
